pr_title: tests: testsuite: add emulating send IPI in X2APIC mode
pr_body:
We emulate the interrupt by sending the IPI to core itself by
the local APIC for x86 platfrom.

But in X2APIC mode, this no longer works. So we emulate the
interrupt the by writing the IA32_X2APIC_SELF_IPI MSR to send
IPI to the core itself via LOAPIC also. According to SDM vol.3
chapter 10.12.11.

Fixes #42108

Signed-off-by: Enjia Mai <enjia.mai@intel.com>
pr_comments: Hi @andyross , @tbursztyka , @jhedberg, could you please help on review this when you got a chance? Thanks!

I forgot about this header.  Not opposed to this patch, but it seems like it's needless complexity.  The point to having interrupt triggers in the generic test suite is to get coverage of the portable/standard arch layer interrupt entry and exit.  We can do that on x86 with a synchronous INT instruction.

If we want coverage of the deeper IO-/x2/APIC/MSI/MSIx platform layers, then we probably want to have a platform test and not try to do it here.  There is similar madness in tests/kernel/context where our "portable" test does a giant #if tree trying to figure out what the timer IRQ number is.

Hi @andyross , after thinking this more, I think your point is reasonable. This is more general tests for interrupt, and if we just verify the interrupt trigger, using INT here is enough. The reason I change to use IPI is I also want to test irq_disable() and irq_lock(), but as you mentioned, this is more suitable to put in the tests/arch, either the regular_isr and direct_isr for x86. 

So I will try to make some change and move these tests into arch dependent tests, any further suggestion here? thanks!
Hi @tbursztyka , I have addressed your comments, could you please review it again? thanks!

Hi @andyross , maybe we can merge this first to address the #42108 first, then I will follow what you suggested, to clean up the interrupt tests, make this testsuite more generic and simple (just using INT to trigger interrupt), then move the arch-dependent portion to tests/arch(such as using IPI to test).  This will make thing easier, I prefer doing it this way, do you think that it ok? Thanks!
